text:
Alicia: quick heads-up — ran a skim experiment this morning: enabled KV prefetch + KV-only INT8 quant on the 13B bring-up. Short summary: memory for KV buffers down ~28%, steady-state p50 latency +2%, cold-start p95 +6%. no obvious quality regressions on our dev eval. sharing numbers below.

Mike: nice. can you paste the exact command/config so i can repro locally? also which quant backend (gptq/awq/custom)?

Alicia: used the internal int8-kv path (kernel: kv_int8_dequant_v2), not full-gptq. command: ```./run_infer --model redwood-13b --seq-len 1024 --batch 1 --quant-kv int8 --kv-prefetch true --runs 500 --pin-kv true``` config flags: `kv_prefetch=true`, `kv_quant_mode=int8`, `kv_pin=true`, `dequant_batch=128`

Suresh: thanks. did you measure token-level delta or perplexity on the eval prompts? any hallucination uptick?

Alicia: ran the standard onboarding eval (1k samples, coding+wiki+dialog). metrics: token-accuracy delta ~ -0.3% (top1 tokens), perplexity +0.6%. for long-context QA we saw a tiny drop in span-extraction F1 (-0.4). qualitatively we saw 2/1k responses with mild tokenization artifacts on headings. overall seems within noise but worth A/B.

Emily: can you share RAM/GPU mem snapshots? curious about buffer vs model weight savings.

Alicia: memory traces attached inline — summarized: GPU resident reduced from 14.2GB -> 10.2GB (KV region contribution). Host pinned KV buffer down from 3.1GB -> 2.2GB. CPU RSS unchanged. cold-start heap bump observed while dequantizing (~120ms spike).

Jordan: that cold p95 bump smells like dequant done synchronously on first access. can we async prefetch+dequant or limit prefetch depth? prefetch=true might be eager for long prefixes. suggest `kv_prefetch_depth=64` or async dequant task.

Alicia: good call. i tried `kv_prefetch_depth=64` locally — p95 cold dropped from +6% -> +3% and steady-state unchanged. async dequant prototype reduced cold spike further but adds complexity.

Mike: any ops/kernel hotspots from perfviz?

Alicia: perf trace: top hotspots are `kv_dequant` (45ms aggregated over batch) and `kv_copy_async` (22ms). backend math kernels unaffected. attaching sample flame (paste): ```KV_DEQUANT 45ms; KV_COPY_ASYNC 22ms; ATTENTION_KERNEL 18ms```

Suresh: for rollout, i'd vote for hybrid: INT8 for attention key/value only, keep value proj or final dense fp16. that should save most KV memory while reducing dequant noise. can we run a quick shadow traffic mix?

Alicia: agreed. plan: 1) run hybrid-int8-kv (keys/vals int8, value-proj fp16) w/ `kv_prefetch_depth=64` 2) run 10k-sample eval for regressions 3) nightly perf job to capture tails. i'll queue them.

ci-bot: nightly-perf job queued: perf-job-2105678901-hybrid-int8-kv; will post results to this thread when done :robot_face:

Mike: i'll help with the shadow rollout script and infra config. ping me when ci-bot posts. :thumbsup:

Emily: also capture rollback metric (latency vs token-quality) so product can set a safe SLO threshold.

Alicia: yep — adding a quick dashboard: p50/p95 latency, KV memory, token-accuracy delta, sample failing prompts. thanks all.

Jordan: one more note — if we plan on fp8 in future, keep the dequant path modular so we can swap kernels. avoid coupling to int8-only helpers.

Alicia: noted. i'll include kernel abstraction in the PR. end of thread.
